title: Reward Model Perspectives: Whose Opinions Do Reward Models Reward?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating reward model alignment with age-specific human opinions and measuring preference for age-related stereotypes using multiple-choice responses from OpinionQA, PRISM, and BBQ datasets.
Comparing reward model scores on stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical multiple-choice statements involving disability status using the BBQ dataset.
Measuring reward model stereotyping rates and opinion alignment across gender demographics by analyzing reward scores on multiple-choice questions from BBQ, StereoSet, PRISM, and OpinionQA.
Evaluating reward model preference for stereotypes involving different nationalities using context-question pairs from the BBQ dataset.
Testing reward model preferences for stereotypical versus non-stereotypical statements regarding physical appearance using the BBQ benchmark.
Assessing reward model opinion alignment and stereotyping rates across racial and ethnic groups using reward distributions on multiple-choice queries from OpinionQA, PRISM, BBQ, and StereoSet.

Evaluating opinion alignment and stereotyping preferences across religious identities by calculating reward model score distances against demographic baselines using OpinionQA, PRISM, BBQ, and StereoSet.
Measuring reward model preference scores for stereotypical associations related to sexual orientation using the BBQ dataset.
Comparing reward model alignment with survey responses stratified by income, education, and employment status using OpinionQA and PRISM, as well as evaluating SES stereotypes in BBQ.

Evaluating reward model opinion alignment with specific political parties and ideologies by computing distance metrics (like Wasserstein distance) between model reward distributions and human survey data from OpinionQA.
Testing reward model preferences for professional stereotypes by identifying the highest reward scores across stereotyped, anti-stereotyped, and unrelated text using the StereoSet dataset.
